b25a1fe384a0.title: Personas
b25a1fe384a0.content: . Authoring Personas . SMART Guidelines and Digital Adaptation Kits (DAKs) are authored by multidisciplinary teams. The authoring personas defined here represent the roles involved in the authoring, review, and publication lifecycle — distinct from the clinical/health personas defined within a DAK itself. These personas are derived from the WHO SMART IG Starter Kit guidance on DAK development teams, authoring processes, and community of practice workstreams. Persona Definitions . | Persona | Description | Primary Phase | . | Programme Manager | Manages DAK scope, timeline, resources, and stakeholder engagement | Planning | . | Technical Officer | Coordinates DAK work and performs first-pass content review | Planning, L2 Review | . | Clinical SME | Validates clinical accuracy against L1 guidelines | L2 Review | . | Business Analyst | Authors L2 DAK components (BPMN, data dictionary, logic, requirements) | L2 Authoring | . | FHIR Modeller | Authors L3 FHIR artifacts from L2 specifications | L3 Authoring | . | Terminologist | Manages terminology, concept mappings, and WHO Commons dictionary | L3 Authoring, Governance | . | QC Reviewer | Reviews publication readiness using checklists and QA reports | Quality Control | . | Content Reviewer | Approves content at decision gates (L2→L3, draft→publication) | Review / Approval | . | Publication Manager | Manages IG configuration, builds, versioning, and releases | Publication | . | Translator | Translates IG content across UN languages | Translation | . RASCI Matrix . The IG Starter Kit recommends defining a RASCI (Responsible, Accountable, Support, Consulted, Informed) matrix. Below is a reference matrix mapping personas to lifecycle phases: . | Phase | Programme Manager | Technical Officer | Clinical SME | Business Analyst | FHIR Modeller | Terminologist | QC Reviewer | Content Reviewer | Publication Manager | Translator | . | Planning | A/R | S | C | C | I | I | I | I | I | I | . | L2 Authoring | S | A | C | R | I | C | I | I | I | I | . | Clinical Review | I | S | A/R | S | I | I | I | C | I | I | . | L3 Authoring | I | I | C | S | A/R | R | I | I | S | I | . | Quality Control | I | I | C | S | S | S | A/R | S | S | I | . | Content Approval | I | I | C | I | S | I | S | A/R | I | I | . | Translation | I | I | C | I | S | I | S | I | I | A/R | . | Publication | I | I | I | I | S | I | S | S | A/R | I | . Legend: R = Responsible, A = Accountable, S = Support, C = Consulted, I = Informed . Relationship to DAK Personas . These authoring personas should not be confused with DAK component 2 “Generic Personas” which represent end users of healthcare systems (e.g. Community Health Worker, Healthcare Provider). The authoring personas represent the people who create the SMART Guidelines, while DAK personas represent the people who use the resulting digital systems. Edit this page on GitHub .

23a441a5f76f.title: Process
23a441a5f76f.content: . Authoring Process . The SMART Guidelines authoring lifecycle encompasses DAK development, L3 FHIR authoring, quality control, translation, and publication. This process is defined as a BPMN 2.0 collaboration diagram with swimlanes for each authoring persona. The process is based on the WHO SMART IG Starter Kit guidance. Lifecycle Overview . Phase 1 Phase 2a Phase 2b Phase 3 Phase 4 PLANNING → L2 DAK → L3 FHIR → QUALITY → PUBLICATION AUTHORING AUTHORING CONTROL Programme Business FHIR QC Publication Manager Analyst Modeller Reviewer Manager Clinical SME Terminologist Translator Technical Officer . Phase 1: Planning (Programme Manager) . | Scoping — Define DAK purpose, target audience, and gaps | Form team — Assemble DAK development team (<10 people), define RASCI matrix | Establish process — Select Agile/Scrum methodology and project tooling | Gather source documents — Collect WHO guidelines, registers, policy documents | Plan timeline — Draft project roadmap, create backlog, set sprint cadence | Plan consultations — Schedule SME consultation format and frequency | Assign work — Begin sprint cycle | . Phase 2a: L2 DAK Authoring (Business Analyst, iterative) . The L2 authoring follows an iterative sprint cycle of Fill → Validate → Incorporate: . | Review L1 source documents for current sprint scope | Identify health interventions and recommendations (Component 1) | Author generic personas (Component 2) | Author user scenarios (Component 3) | Author BPMN business processes (Component 4) | For each business process: . | Draft detailed workflow annotations | Define core data elements (Component 5) | Develop decision-support logic (Component 6) | Develop scheduling logic (Component 7) | List indicators and metrics (Component 8) | Define functional/non-functional requirements (Component 9) | . | Streamline all DAK components for cross-component consistency | Validate with SMEs (Clinical SME review) | Incorporate feedback and begin next sprint | . Clinical Review (Clinical SME) . | Validate DAK components against L1 recommendations | Ground-truth with field practice (country visits, facility interviews) | Provide clinical feedback and identify gaps | . Phase 2b: L3 FHIR Authoring (FHIR Modeller) . | Verify L2 input availability and consistency | Set up IG repository from smart-ig-empty template | Author L3 artifacts in recommended sequence: . | Logical Models → Profiles → Questionnaires → StructureMaps | CodeSystems, ValueSets, ConceptMaps (with Terminologist) | CQL (decision logic, scheduling, indicators) | PlanDefinitions (processes, decision tables) | ActorDefinitions (reusing Commons repository) | Measures, Requirements, Scenarios, Tests | . | Run IG Publisher build and fix issues iteratively | . Terminology Management (Terminologist, concurrent with L3) . | Review terminology bindings and code systems | Map concepts to WHO Commons dictionary | Map to ICD-11, SNOMED CT, LOINC | Onboard new concepts through governance process | . Phase 3: Quality Control (QC Reviewer) . | Review QA report (qa.html) from IG Publisher | Review checklist items across L1, L2, L3, L4, Global sections | Validate artifact conformance to CRMI profiles | Test L3 functionality (StructureMaps, CQL, Measures) | Decision gate: Publication ready? . | No: Report issues to FHIR Modeller for resolution → re-review | Yes: Approve for publication | . | Review translated content for completeness | . Translation (Translator, concurrent with QC) . | Translate narrative and resource metadata | Create example resources per UN language | Submit translations for QC review | . Phase 4: Publication (Publication Manager) . | Review changes since last release, determine version number | Optionally create release-candidate branch | Update IG status — status=active, version=X.Y.Z, releaseLabel=release | Create publication-request.json | Run final build and verify | Create GitHub release and tag (vX.Y.Z) — triggers automated workflow | Verify automated publication succeeded (sitepreview) | Request WHO team to update smart.who.int | Reset main to draft, update version for next cycle | . BPMN Process Diagram . The formal BPMN 2.0 process diagram is available at: SGAuthoring.DAKLifecycle.bpmn (with the other authoring processes under smart-base/processes/) . This diagram models the full lifecycle as a collaboration with swimlanes for each authoring persona, including message flows between participants for handoffs (e.g. Business Analyst → Clinical SME for validation, QC Reviewer → Publication Manager for approval). Edit this page on GitHub .

67072b12cc09.title: Skills
67072b12cc09.content: . Authoring Skills . Each authoring skill is modeled as a FHIR Requirements resource conforming to the SGRequirements profile. Each skill states a capability (e.g. “Can review terminology”) and contains checklist statements that define the criteria for demonstrating that capability. Skills are organized by domain and assigned to authoring personas to define each persona’s skill package. Skill Inventory . Content Review Skills . | Skill | Description | Personas | . | Can review and approve content | Review and formally approve content at decision gates | Content Reviewer | . Project Management Skills . | Skill | Description | Personas | . | Can scope DAK | Define DAK scope, source documents, and development process | Programme Manager | . | Can manage stakeholders | Engage SMEs, coordinate consultations, manage RASCI | Programme Manager, Technical Officer | . | Can plan iterations | Plan sprints, maintain backlog, facilitate retrospectives | Programme Manager | . BPMN Swimlane Validation . As part of the BPMN authoring and review process, every innermost swimlane in a BPMN diagram SHALL correspond to an ActorDefinition resource. A lane names its ActorDefinition by id: its partitionElementRef (a top-level <bpmn:resource> whose id is the ActorDefinition’s FSH Instance: id), or else its own id. A lane is never matched by its display name or by a file name. The bpmn-validate tool in the smart-base knowledge graph checks this, together with the diagram’s structure and the absence of Camunda or Zeebe extensions, on every pull request that changes a .bpmn. When a swimlane has no matching ActorDefinition, the author must resolve by: . | Referencing an ActorDefinition from a dependency IG | Creating a new ActorDefinition in this IG | Correcting the lane’s binding (its partitionElementRef or id) | . e9fe1bbb341f.title: SMART Base
e9fe1bbb341f.content: . Overview . WHO SMART Guidelines (Standards-based, Machine-readable, Adaptive, Requirements-based, and Testable) are a set of WHO clinical guidelines that have been transformed into a computable, interoperable format. They enable countries to rapidly adopt, adapt, and implement WHO recommendations within their digital health systems by providing structured, machine-readable clinical content. A Digital Adaptation Kit (DAK) is the primary artefact of WHO SMART Guidelines. It is a structured, standardised package of clinical and operational content that represents a WHO health intervention in a computable form. Each DAK contains: . | Health interventions and recommendations – the clinical guidance from WHO | Generic personas – representative end-users and actors in the health system | User scenarios – narrative descriptions of how the guidance is used in practice | Business processes and workflows – step-by-step care pathways | Core data elements – the data dictionary for the health domain | Decision-support logic – computable clinical decision rules | Functional and non-functional requirements – system capability requirements | Program indicators – aggregate measures and metrics for monitoring and evaluation | Test scenarios – structured tests to validate conformance | . The diagram below illustrates the nine components of a WHO DAK and how they relate to one another: . Figure 1 – The nine components of a WHO Digital Adaptation Kit (DAK) This implementation guide contains base conformance resources for use in all WHO SMART Guidelines implementation guides. Authoring Lifecycle . The DAK authoring lifecycle is a five-phase process spanning planning, L2 DAK authoring, L3 FHIR authoring, quality control, and publication. The BPMN 2.0 collaboration diagram below shows the end-to-end process with swimlanes for each authoring persona. Figure 2 – DAK Authoring Lifecycle (BPMN 2.0). See Authoring Process for details. See the SMART IG Starter Kit for more information on building and using WHO SMART Guidelines. DAK (Digital Adaptation Kit) URL Handling . For repositories whose root index.config.json declares a DAK (a dak section under contentTypes; formerly a dak.json file), this implementation guide provides enhanced URL handling for publication and preview scenarios: . Publication URLs . | WHO Repositories: For repositories owned by WorldHealthOrganization, the publication URL follows the pattern https://smart.who.int/{stub} where {stub} is the repository name with any smart- prefix removed. | Other Repositories: Use the canonical URL specified in sushi-config.yaml or fall back to GitHub Pages pattern. | . Preview URLs . | All Repositories: Preview URLs use the GitHub Pages pattern https://{profile}.github.io/{repo} for current CI builds. | . Branch-Based URL Selection . | Release Branches (prefixed with release-): Use publication URLs for canonical references and resource identifiers. | Development Branches: Use preview URLs for canonical references and resource identifiers. | . The DAK configuration is automatically regenerated during CI builds to ensure URLs are appropriate for the current branch context. cbafc36bc92f.title: What SMART Base adds to the FHIR IG layer
cbafc36bc92f.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Step | Checkout script | When it runs | What it does | . | DAK pre-processing | smart-base:dak-pre-export (smart-base/scripts/dak-pre-export.sh) | before the Publisher, as the pre-export: of ig-ast-refresh.yml | runs the WHO scripts in input/scripts/ (generate_dak_from_sushi.py, update_sushi_config.py, and, for an IG that declares contentTypes.dak, dmn_questionnaire_generator.py, transform_dmn.py and inject_translations.py) in a Python venv | . | DAK API sidecars | ig-site:sidecars (smart-base/scripts/ig-site-sidecars.ts) | after the AST is restored, when smart-base is the IG’s site.landing | writes the API sidecars from the AST, labelled “DAK API” when the IG declares contentTypes.dak; the FHIR IG layer binds them to the artefact pages | . a35d7e759123.doc: Building and publishing the SMART Base IG
a35d7e759123.title: Render it from the command line
a35d7e759123.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . From a checkout of litlfred/smart-base. On a fresh clone the first bun run cat … mounts the layers index.lock.json pins, then runs the command ("cat": "bun .github/cat.ts"); after a re-pin, bash .github/mount-from-lock.sh remounts them. # See what would be built and where bun run cat stage:local --repo . --plan # Build the site and compose the publish commit; push nothing bun run cat stage:local --repo . --dry-run # Or write a bundle you can open as a page bun run cat stage:local --repo . --artifact ./_preview . The render restores the AST from the cache branch cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/smart.who.int.base, which already holds one. When the AST is stale (you changed input/, sushi-config.yaml or ig.ini), rebuild it with the DAK pre-processing by starting the repository’s IG AST refresh workflow (.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml) on your branch. Running bun run cat prepare:fhir-harness on your machine builds an AST without the DAK pre-processing, because that script does not run a pre-export step. Use it only to check that the FSH compiles. The content gate. Before it composes the site, the render checks every narrative, markdown field and page for injection attempts. It needs an agent review of exactly that content in qa/ig-content-qa.json. When the IG’s content changes, the review goes stale and the publish is refused until it is recorded again: . bun run cat ig-content-qa:scan # what the reviewer reads bun run cat ig-content-qa:record --reviewer <who> # update qa/ig-content-qa.json . For a local look only, IG_CONTENT_QA_ACCEPT_UNREVIEWED=1 skips a missing or stale review. The steps are the ig-content-qa skill. To run the DAK pre-processing on its own, for example to inspect what it writes: bun run cat smart-base:dak-pre-export. It changes files under input/; restore them with git checkout -- input sushi-config.yaml before you commit.

9e54eae5a738.doc: Building and publishing the SMART Base IG
9e54eae5a738.title: The plain WHO build, with the IG Publisher alone
9e54eae5a738.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . This repository keeps the files of the stock WHO build, which runs the IG Publisher with no harness: . | Command | What it does | . | ./_updatePublisher.sh | downloads the latest publisher.jar, so the version floats | . | ./_genonce.sh | runs the Publisher once over the IG; the HTML is in output/ | . | ./_gencontinuous.sh | runs it again on every change | . In CI the same build is .github/workflows/ghbuild.yml: six DAK pre-processing steps, the Publisher, then nine post-processing steps that write the DAK API, the JSON Schemas and the JSON-LD vocabularies. bun run cat stage:local --repo . --bare-ig publishes that output as it is. Use this route to compare with WHO’s own build. The harnessed site above is what this repository publishes.

a4a0242edfdf.doc: Building and publishing the SMART Base IG
a4a0242edfdf.title: The publishing pipeline
a4a0242edfdf.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . To release, the owner tags the version in sushi-config.yaml as v<version> on main and pushes the tag. The steps are the FHIR IG layer’s Releasing. A merged pull request publishes the site. A push to main that changes input/, sushi-config.yaml or ig.ini refreshes the AST, and every push to main republishes the site. The publish waits for that commit’s AST refresh ("publishAfter": ["ig-ast-refresh.yml"] in index.config.json). Previews of other branches, and every other workflow here, are started by hand from the Actions tab. | Workflow | What it does | . | ig-ast-refresh.yml | on a push to main that changes the IG’s inputs, and by hand. Calls the FHIR IG layer’s reusable refresh, with pre-export: bash smart-base/scripts/dak-pre-export.sh and the WHO template. Seeds the AST cache from main | . | site-publish.yml | on every push to main, and by hand. Calls cat-harness-tools’ reusable folio-site-publish.yml, which mounts the layers and runs stage-local.ts --repo .. On main it publishes the gh-pages root; on another branch, branches/<branch>/ | . | standing-repin.yml | when an upstream layer merges, and by hand: opens one PR that moves the pins a standing consent covers | . | pr-preview.yml | a pull request preview, deployed after a collaborator approves it in the pr-preview environment | . | ghbuild.yml | the plain WHO build (above) | . | ig-release.yml | on a v* tag, and by hand for an existing tag: a full build of the tag with the DAK pre-processing, then a GitHub draft release with package.tgz (and its R4/R4B variants), ast-data.zip and SHA256SUMS. The owner publishes the draft | . | release.yml | by hand, after the draft is published: checks publication-request.json and calls WHO’s publication workflow | . The gh-pages root publish also keeps v0/, ns/, 0.1.0/ and sitepreview/ (site.build.keep in index.config.json): the JSON-LD vocabulary and context that publish-context.yml writes. A root publish that would drop one of them is refused.

db75bb165305.doc: Building and publishing the SMART Base IG
db75bb165305.title: Deployment targets
db75bb165305.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . SMART Base deploys to GitHub Pages only. The options, and what each would take, are on the FHIR IG layer’s page: Deployment targets: GitHub Pages and Cloudflare. Two points are particular to this IG: . | The canonical is http://smart.who.int/base. It names WHO’s publication, not this site, so moving this site to another host or domain does not change the canonical. It does change every link to litlfred.github.io/smart-base/ that is already published. | The site is large, with six languages and an OpenAPI page per operation. Count the files on gh-pages before choosing Cloudflare Pages, which limits the number of files per deployment. | .

41c4fa54cd5f.title: L1–L5: five layers, not five stages; FHIR content is the first three
41c4fa54cd5f.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . WHO SMART Guidelines names five knowledge layers. FHIR content lives in the first three, and those three are the clearest available vocabulary for FHIR content generally: . | layer | what it holds | form | . | L1 Narrative | narrative guidance — the publication a recommendation comes from | prose, figures, tables | . | L2 Operational | the Digital Adaptation Kit — its ten components, from health interventions to test scenarios | BPMN, DMN, structured tables | . | L3 Machine readable | the FHIR Implementation Guide | FSH → FHIR resources | . | L4 Executable | reference applications and services that execute the static algorithms | software | . | L5 Dynamic | dynamic algorithms trained and optimised on data — the precision-health model | models, analytics | . The five names and their meanings are from the WHO Digital transformation handbook for primary health care (2024), §1.2 pp. 20–21 (who-iris/library/9789240093362-eng). Its ref. 18 is the primary source: Mehl G. et al., WHO SMART guidelines: optimising country-level use of guideline recommendations in the digital age, Lancet Digital Health 2021;3(4):e213–e216 (smart-base/library/mehl-2021-who-smart-guidelines, CC BY 3.0 IGO), which presents the same five as “knowledge layers (L1–L5)”. This page stops at L3. L4 and L5 are software and trained models. They consume what L1–L3 publish, but they are not authored as FHIR content, so nothing in this platform validates them as content. They are knowledge layers, not stages. All three are live at once: an L2 decision table and the L3 PlanDefinition derived from it are both published and both can change. Treating L2 as scaffolding that L3 replaces lets the two drift apart unnoticed. A repository layer may also hold any one of the three knowledge layers without the others: an L1 corpus with no DAK, or an IG with no L1. The SMART knowledge layers are not the platform’s layers. cat-harness, the content core and the science layer are layers of this software; each depends on the one before and inherits its skills and directories. L1–L5 are knowledge layers, layers of guideline knowledge. A WHO folio holds L1–L3 content; the platform layers author and check it, and none of them is “the L2 layer”. The deck that sets the two side by side is cat-harness/library/content/kg-folio-asst-2026-09-30 (slide 1).

e3424260bffb.title: The DAK API surface
e3424260bffb.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . A WHO SMART Guidelines IG publishes an extra layer on top of standard IG output — the DAK API — produced by scripts that run after the Publisher exits: . | <stem>.schema.json — a JSON Schema per logical model and per ValueSet | <stem>.displays.json — display labels | <stem>.openapi.json — an OpenAPI description | <stem>.jsonld — a JSON-LD vocabulary, built from ValueSet expansions | dak-api.html — the hub a reader enters through | . Its size varies by two orders of magnitude between IGs; a figure describes one IG at one version. None of this is the Publisher’s work: a missing schema is a question about a post-processing script, not the build. The JSON-LD vocabularies inherit the terminology server’s availability, so a thin vocabulary may mean a thin ValueSet or one nobody could expand, and the artefact alone does not say which.

ef63fe162dda.title: The WHO build around the IG Publisher
ef63fe162dda.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The FHIR IG Publisher and FHIR content in general are described on the FHIR IG Publisher and FHIR content pages of the FHIR IG layer. This section covers what is specific to the WHO SMART Guidelines build. The commands, the publishing pipeline and the published assets are on Building and publishing the SMART Base IG. The Publisher is one step of many. It runs between six pre-processing invocations and nine post-processing ones. The DAK API, the JSON Schemas and the JSON-LD vocabularies are produced after it exits, by scripts. The version floats. The WHO build downloads publisher.jar from the latest release on every run, so two builds of an unchanged commit can differ, and nothing in the output says which version produced them. The dependency closure. For the DAK layer, the Publisher resolves hl7.terminology, hl7.fhir.uv.extensions.r4, hl7.fhir.uv.cql, hl7.fhir.uv.cpg, hl7.fhir.uv.crmi and hl7.fhir.uv.sdc. The rules are skills; where a skill and this page disagree, the skill wins: . | l2-dak-authoring: authoring at L2, and deriving rather than retyping. | ig-artifact-ingestion: reading a published IG back as a knowledge graph: which IGs qualify, what to read, what to refuse, the four partial views and the two traps. | dak-preprocessing and dak-postprocessing: the WHO-specific phases around the Publisher run, step by step. | smart-stack-layering: which harness layer a given asset belongs to, and the question that settles it. | .

This guide covers authoring the L2 artifacts with folio-assistant and an LLM. Skill package: authoring-who-smart-guidelines .

1ff32aac4f41.title: The L2 artifacts
1ff32aac4f41.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… KG… . BPMN 2.0 source · full-size SVG . | Artifact | Skill | Format | . | Business processes | bpmn-authoring | BPMN 2.0 XML | . | Decision logic | dmn-authoring | DMN tables | . | Data dictionary | l2-dak-authoring | Excel / structured | . | Terminology | terminology-management | code systems / value sets | . | Review | content-review | criteria-based | . The table lists authoring skills, not the DAK. A DAK has ten components: the original eight, plus scheduling logic (split out of decision-support logic) and test scenarios. Against the skills above: . | # | DAK component | covered above by | . | 1 | Health interventions and recommendations | — (cites L1) | . | 2 | Generic personas | — | . | 3 | User scenarios | — | . | 4 | Business processes and workflows | bpmn-authoring | . | 5 | Core data elements | l2-dak-authoring, terminology-management | . | 6 | Decision-support logic | dmn-authoring | . | 7 | Scheduling logic | dmn-authoring (decision tables) | . | 8 | Indicators and monitoring | — | . | 9 | Functional and non-functional requirements | — | . | 10 | Test scenarios | — | . A dash means no skill in this table, not no skill anywhere: look before starting that component. Scheduling logic is authored, but not yet formalized. It is written as DMN decision tables, like decision-support logic, but has no L2 logical-model field or L3 artefact of its own yet. The sources count differently: . | WHO’s DAK figure (slide 3 of cat-harness/library/content/kg-folio-asst-2026-09-30) shows nine cards, with scheduling logic as #7, and testing drawn beside them; its speaker notes say eight. | The SMART Base DAK logical model (DAK.fsh) declares nine fields: test scenarios in, and scheduling logic carried inside decision-support logic. | WHO’s IG starter kit, L2 DAK authoring (https://smart.who.int/ig-starter-kit/l2_dak_authoring.html; source input/pagecontent/l2_dak_authoring.md in WorldHealthOrganization/smart-ig-starter-kit) disagrees with itself: its introduction counts “9 interlinked components” with scheduling logic as #7 and no testing; its table counts 9 with test scenarios as #9 and scheduling logic inside decision-support logic. | . This repository encodes ten. DAK_COMPONENTS in smart-base/schemas/dak-kinds.ts lists ten and names scheduling logic in DAK_UNFORMALIZED_COMPONENTS: its field name is ready (schedulingLogic), but DAK.fsh does not declare it yet. The other nine are checked against DAK.fsh field for field.

0575cb56f50e.title: Workflow
0575cb56f50e.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Plan — content-plan: enumerate the processes, decisions, and data elements the guideline implies; identify actors (business analyst, clinical SME, terminologist). | Author business processes — ask the agent to draft BPMN for each clinical workflow (bpmn-authoring); it produces valid BPMN 2.0. | Author decision logic — capture recommendations as DMN decision tables (dmn-authoring), linked to the data dictionary. | Author the data dictionary — define core data elements with types, cardinality, and terminology bindings (l2-dak-authoring). | Manage terminology — define code systems / value sets and bind them (terminology-management). | Validate & review — content-validate then content-review against the DAK criteria. | .

ff34e9ad26b5.title: A mock session
ff34e9ad26b5.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . You: Plan the L2 DAK for the immunization guideline — I need the “administer vaccine” process and the “is the client due” decision. Assistant: (loads content-plan) Proposed: 1 BPMN process administer-vaccine, 1 DMN decision client-due-for-vaccine, 4 core data elements (client id, antigen, dose number, date administered), 1 value set (antigen codes). Scaffold it? . You: Yes. Assistant: (loads bpmn-authoring, dmn-authoring, l2-dak-authoring) Created the BPMN with start → check eligibility → administer → record, the DMN table keyed on age/last-dose, and the data dictionary. (calls content_validate) All artifacts valid.

2c898e461133.title: Prerequisites
2c898e461133.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The L3 toolchain is heavier than the platform baseline. The authoring-who-smart-guidelines package’s Docker manifest provisions it; to run locally you need: . | Tool | Purpose | Install | . | Java 21 (JRE) | IG Publisher | apt install openjdk-21-jre-headless | . | FHIR IG Publisher | build the IG | download publisher.jar from HL7/fhir-ig-publisher | . | SUSHI (fsh-sushi) | compile FSH → FHIR | npm i -g fsh-sushi | . | Jekyll | IG site rendering | gem install jekyll bundler | . Run bun run cat check-deps and the agent’s check_dependencies tool to confirm. These are the tools of the plain IG Publisher build. To render an IG through the harness, which builds the site from the Publisher’s AST and pins its versions, see Building and publishing the SMART Base IG.

48499dbee18c.title: Making the build incremental
48499dbee18c.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… KG… . BPMN 2.0 source · full-size SVG . On the immunizations IG the median artefact has no dependents and the 90th percentile has six, so almost every edit invalidates a handful of resources and the index. The build therefore rebuilds only the change’s dependency cone where it can. The process above is the L3 pipeline’s build lane with the derived artefacts cached by dependency cone. Restore the cache; compute the change’s cone with bun run fhir-harness/scripts/fsh-cone.ts <ig-root> --changed <files>; compile and validate only the cone against the warm validator; re-render the cone’s records; rebuild the meta-index; assemble the site. A cache miss or a moved toolchain falls back to a full build, and only a green build of main or a release seeds the cache. A release is always cut from a full build. The rules are fhir-harness’s ig-build-pipeline skill. | Step | Implemented by | . | Restore and seed the derived state | fhir-harness/scripts/ig-cache.sh (restore, verify, seed) | . | Compute the cone of the change | fhir-harness/scripts/fsh-cone.ts | . | Validate the cone | fhir-validation over the warm validator service (proposed MCP tools) | . | Rebuild the meta-index, assemble the site | ig_metaindex_rebuild (proposed), ig-publication | . | QC gates, deploy | quality-control, content-publish | .
